code_label: Real-time arbitrage is speed-constrained
text_span: short-lived price discrepancies require real-time, high-speed processing of vast solution space, posing challenges for classical computing.
rationale: States the motivating problem constraint and why the task is difficult.

code_label: Simple-cycle constraints improve validity
text_span: adding simple cycle preservation constraints, which guarantee trading cycle validity and eliminate redundant or infeasible substructures.
rationale: Summarizes the main modeling enhancement introduced by the paper.

code_label: Multiple solvers are benchmarked
text_span: we use and benchmark various solvers, including Quantum Annealing (QA), gate-based quantum approaches such as Variational Quantum Algorithm with Adaptive Cost Encoding (ACE), as well as classical solvers such as Gurobi and classical meta heuristics such as Tabu Search (TS).
rationale: Identifies the comparative evaluation design across solver families.

code_label: Multi-bit swap post-processing is proposed
text_span: We propose a classical multi-bit swap post-processing to improve the solution generated by ACE.
rationale: Captures the additional local-search refinement step.

code_label: Execution time and profit are key metrics
text_span: we compare these methods in terms of both arbitrage profit and execution time, the two key performance metrics.
rationale: Defines the evaluation criteria used throughout the study.

code_label: Quantum methods are assessed for financial use
text_span: Our results give insight into the current capabilities and limitations of quantum methods for real-time financial use cases.
rationale: States the broader interpretive aim of the empirical comparison.

code_label: Prior work lacked simple-cycle preservation
text_span: none of the models includes the simple-cycle preservation constraints, which ensure no repeated currencies except at the start and end position of the arbitrage cycle.
rationale: Identifies a gap in prior currency arbitrage formulations.

code_label: No prior benchmark on real-world data
text_span: no prior work has benchmarked quantum techniques against strong classical baselines using real-world currency exchange data for currency arbitrage optimization problem.
rationale: Claims novelty in benchmarking on real-world exchange data.

code_label: Enhanced model enforces feasibility and uniqueness
text_span: introducing constraints that preserve simple-cycle within arbitrage opportunity. This addition ensures the feasibility and uniqueness of cycles identified by solvers
rationale: States the intended effect of the new constraints.

code_label: Node-based formulation avoids extra variables
text_span: The proposed mathematical model employs a node-based formulation, enabling the incorporation of simple-cycle preservation (sub-tour elimination) constraints without introducing additional variables.
rationale: Describes a structural modeling choice and its advantage.

code_label: Edge-based formulation may be infeasible
text_span: the edge-based formulation presented in [9] does not account for this constraint, which may result in infeasible arbitrage cycles.
rationale: States a caveat about an alternative formulation.

code_label: Real-world data and multiple solvers are used
text_span: We solve this model using a range of solvers- quantum annealing, gate-based quantum hybrid method (ACE) [8], and classical solvers (Gurobi and Tabu Search).
rationale: Summarizes the solution approaches used in the study.

code_label: ACE results are improved by local search
text_span: We introduce multi bit swap as classical local search post-processing technique on the results from ACE to improve solution quality.
rationale: Captures the post-processing contribution.

code_label: Execution latency is critical for arbitrage
text_span: emphasizing execution latency as a critical factor for practical arbitrage.
rationale: Highlights the practical performance requirement motivating the work.

code_label: Simple-cycle preservation is modeled without extra variables
text_span: Our model formulates the arbitrage problem as a binary quadratic programming (BQP) problem, incorporating transaction costs and market constraints, and is designed to be compatible with both quantum and classical optimization techniques
rationale: Describes the modeling framework and compatibility goal.

code_label: Binary variables encode currency positions
text_span: Decision variables: xi,k = (1, if currency i is in the kth position in the cycle 0, otherwise
rationale: Defines the core decision variable representation.

code_label: Objective minimizes negative log exchange rates
text_span: min X i,j∈V K X k=1 −log(wi,j) · xi,kxj,k+1
rationale: States the optimization objective used to find profitable cycles.

code_label: Position assignment constraint
text_span: N X i=1 xi,k = 1, ∀1 ≤ k ≤ K
rationale: Captures the constraint that each cycle position has exactly one currency.

code_label: Currency uniqueness constraint
text_span: K X k=1 xi,k ≤ 1, ∀1 ≤ i ≤ N
rationale: Captures the constraint that each currency appears at most once.

code_label: Non-edge adjacency is forbidden
rationale: Ensures only valid exchange links can appear consecutively.

code_label: Cycle closure constraint
rationale: Ensures the cycle returns to the starting currency.

code_label: QUBO penalty terms encode constraints
text_span: the second, third, fourth and fifth term of the above equation are the corresponding penalty terms of constraints eq.(2), eq.(3), eq.(4), eq.(5) respectively
rationale: Explains how the constrained model is converted into QUBO.

code_label: Penalty weights are chosen by VLM
text_span: We have used Verma and Lewis Method (VLM) [10] to find the optimal values of λ1, λ2, λ3 and λ4.
rationale: States the method used to set penalty coefficients.

code_label: QA uses annealing to reach low-energy states
text_span: Quantum annealing operates qubits through a preset annealing schedule, which initializes with a Hamiltonian which is easy-to-solve and changes slowly to problem Hamiltonian by using adiabatic theorem [11].
rationale: Describes the QA mechanism used in the study.

code_label: ACE reduces qubit requirements
text_span: the number of qubits reduce to ⌈log2(n)⌉+ 1.
rationale: States the qubit-efficiency claim of ACE.

code_label: ACE uses register and ancilla qubits
text_span: ⌈log2(n)⌉ register qubits encode the state indices and an ancilla qubit represents the binary value corresponding to each state.
rationale: Explains the encoding structure of ACE.

code_label: Local search checks feasibility and objective
text_span: If the flip enhance the objective value and ensures feasibility, the change is retained; otherwise, it is reverted.
rationale: Describes the acceptance rule for the post-processing search.

code_label: Local search complexity is quadratic
text_span: the total complexity of the entire round is thus O(n2).
rationale: Provides the stated computational complexity of the local search.

code_label: ACE training and execution are separated
text_span: the blue dotted line represents the training phase of the ACE circuit with training data to determine its optimal parameters, while the green solid line depicts the execution phase
rationale: Describes the workflow separating parameter training from execution.

code_label: Real-time exchange data is used
text_span: The experimental analysis utilizes a real time currency exchange rate data [13].
rationale: Identifies the empirical data source used in experiments.

code_label: Zero entries indicate missing direct exchange
text_span: The exchange rates which show 0 indicate there is no direct exchange between those currencies.
rationale: Clarifies how missing edges in the data are represented.

code_label: Problem sizes beyond ten are infeasible
text_span: From 11 onwards it is not feasible to generate the arbitrage from the given data.
rationale: States a data-driven feasibility limit in the experiments.

code_label: Circuit 2 with DE performs best in ACE experiments
text_span: we observed that DE performs quite well compared to other optimizers in all problem sizes.
rationale: Reports the optimizer comparison outcome.

code_label: Chosen ACE configuration
text_span: we have used Circuit 2 with two layers, and DE as classical optimizer to find the optimal arbitrage opportunity.
rationale: States the selected ACE setup for subsequent results.

code_label: Profit is measured in pips
text_span: The profit values have been calculated in pip where 1 pip = .0001 difference in price
rationale: Defines the profit metric used in the results table.

code_label: QA and ACE-LS are competitive on small problems
text_span: QA, ACE-LS performs quite well with respect to classical solvers and provides optimal output on small problems which are benchmarked with Gurobi.
rationale: Summarizes the small-instance performance comparison.

code_label: QA and ACE-LS are not always best on larger problems
text_span: these approaches provide profit on large problems but not the best one
rationale: Notes a performance limitation on larger instances.

code_label: QA and ACE-LS are faster than classical solvers
text_span: We observed QA and ACE-LS take less time than classical solvers.
rationale: Reports the main runtime comparison result.

code_label: QA and ACE-LS scale linearly while Gurobi grows exponentially
text_span: It scales linearly with problem size whereas Gurobi grows exponentially.
rationale: States the observed scaling behavior across solvers.

code_label: Execution time is critical in real-time arbitrage
text_span: In currency arbitrage execution time is critical, and QA and ACE-LS can be considered as an initial step toward an industry-level quantum solution.
rationale: Connects the empirical runtime findings to practical deployment relevance.

code_label: Microsecond to millisecond latency remains a challenge
text_span: real-time currency arbitrage demands execution within microseconds to milliseconds, achievable with HPC systems using parallel computing across CPUs, GPUs, and often FPGAs with ultra-low latency infrastructure.
rationale: States a practical latency requirement and contrasts it with current approaches.

code_label: Future work targets real hardware validation
text_span: Future research will focus on executing ACE-LS on real quantum hardware to validate its performance on a practical level.
rationale: Identifies a planned next step for validation.

code_label: Future work seeks better hybrid algorithms
text_span: Investigating advanced hybrid classical-quantum algorithms to further reduce the execution times and improve the solution quality.
rationale: States a future research direction for improving performance.

code_label: Future work explores quantum local search
text_span: we can explore the LS approach in quantum domain, so that the classical overhead can be reduced for improving solution quality.
rationale: Proposes moving the local search component into the quantum domain.

code_label: Neutral atom hardware is proposed for future scaling
text_span: the proposed approach for currency arbitrage can be solved on neutral atom-based quantum computers, leveraging their scalability and long coherence times.
rationale: Names a future hardware platform and rationale.
